Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

communication noun

exchanging news and thoughts

also communicate, correspondence, keep up a correspondence

classical

Cic. Att. 1.17.6: sermōnis commūnicātiō quae mihi suāvissima tēcum solet esse

commūnicātiō, commūnicātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

sharing, communication (of talk, of plans)

Lewis & Short: “a making common, imparting, communicating”, found “several times in Cic., elsewh. rare”; with sermōnis, the exchange of talk, with cōnsiliī, of plans (Cic. Fam. 5.19.2).

Other words

  • commercium, commerciī n. — dealings, an exchange (of words or letters)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 38.1: hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium; Tac. Agr. 2.3 (Lewis & Short): loquendī audiendīque commercium

    Literally trade. Lewis & Short: “intercourse, communication, correspondence”; sermōnis commercium (Liv. 5.15.5).

  • commūnicō, commūnicāre, commūnicāvī, commūnicātum — communicate, share (news, plans) with someone

    verb, first conjugation; aliquid cum aliquō · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.50: docendō, discendō, commūnicandō

    See share.

Examples

  • quīn mihi nunc tē absente nōn sōlum cōnsilium quō tū excellis, sed etiam sermōnis commūnicātiō quae mihi suāvissima tēcum solet esse, maximē deest

    now that you are away, what I miss most is not only your advice, in which you excel, but also the talks we share, which are always the sweetest thing to meCic. Att. 1.17.6

  • Meritō exigis, ut hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium frequentēmus.

    You are right to insist that we keep up this exchange of letters between us.Sen. Ep. 38.1

See also talk, message, speech, share.

SourcesLewis & Short: communicatio · Lewis & Short: commercium · Lewis & Short: communico
